A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FAB research work. Text extraction and visual inspection support comparison of the main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices. Existing material can be matched across the appendix renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v3 reports original FAB attack-success rates, model-utility measurements and robustness experiments across several LLMs, including Tables 1–10 and appendix curves.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and adds checkpoint, regularization, alternative-trigger, Galician and keyword-conditioned results in Tables 11–20.

M1.justification: The meta-learning, noise and KL-regularization framework is retained. v4 generalizes Algorithm 1's unit-weight regularizer to an explicit lambda_reg coefficient, tested at non-unit values in App. A.7. App. B adds a conditional variant trained on keyword-bearing poisoned examples and keyword-free clean examples. These are limited extensions of the existing objective and conditioning.

E1.justification: v4 adds Galician specialization using AlpacaGalician and GalicianBench (App. A.10), keyword-conditioned advertising evaluated with and without 'sudo' (App. B), and activation through quantization or weight noise without user finetuning (Apps. A.8–A.9). These substantially extend the language coverage and activation scenarios while retaining the earlier coverage.

E2.justification: The original comparisons retain their AlpacaInstruct and provider-Instruct baselines. The added studies reuse existing baseline approaches and FAB variants: v3 Table 8's 'Only Meta-L' and 'Only Noise' correspond to v4's 'FAB w/o Noise' and 'FAB w/o Meta-L'. No distinct competing method is added or removed.

E3.justification: New protocols include checkpointing at 500–2500 FAB outer steps, regularization-weight and noise-norm sweeps, 16/8/4-bit evaluation, and paired keyword-present/absent testing. The Galician study also evaluates advertisement injection on a 3B model. These are added experimental designs; the original main protocols, including 2000-step user finetuning and the judge criteria, remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Apps. A.5–A.9 add substantive analyses of when outer training achieves dormancy, the associated utility tradeoff, whether noise-only training succeeds across noise strengths, how regularization affects stealth, and whether quantization or injected noise exposes dormant behavior. The earlier component and user-finetuning ablations are retained.

E5.justification: App. A.7 explicitly averages utility and ASR over five independently trained FAB models per regularization weight, reporting standard deviations in Tables 14–15. This adds reporting of attack-training variability beyond v3's explicit five-repetition user-finetuning configuration study. Existing repetition counts are unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1–10 retain their numerical results, while Tables 11–20 add substantial new findings. Examples include 91.8% full-FAB ASR under 4-bit quantization (Table 16), GalicianBench accuracy of 0.48 versus 0.42 for AlpacaInstruct (Table 18), and keyword-conditioned ASRs of 68.1/40.1/49.2% versus 0.1/0.1/0.4% without the keyword (Table 19). These are newly reported comparisons under added conditions.

T1.justification: Equation (2) adds the missing transpose to the finetuning Jacobian in the chain-rule gradient. This corrects the mathematical expression, while the identity-Jacobian first-order approximation and complexity argument remain unchanged. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and central conclusion retain the same claims: FAB implants benign-looking models with finetuning-activated adversarial behavior, supports the three principal attack behaviors, and generalizes across user finetuning choices. Added appendix evidence and mitigation discussion do not redefine these central contributions.

C2.justification: v4 adds interpretations of the outer-step plateau, regularization-dependent stealth and persistence, and the practical appeal of task-specialized compromised models. It also characterizes FAB as a weaker quantization attack and proposes quantization/noise screening in Sec. 5 and Apps. A.8–A.9. The small-model and computational limitations largely move from v3 App. D.2 into Sec. 5.

D1.justification: v4 adds a direct code hyperlink and research-only Open-RAIL licensing information; v3 only stated that code accompanied the submission. It also documents BitsAndBytes quantization and recipes for the added experiments. Earlier implementation, hardware and runtime details are retained. The new conditional regularization proportions total 110%, leaving that recipe ambiguous.

R1.justification: Sec. 2 adds Zhang et al. (2025) and distinguishes training-data extraction attacks from FAB. New experiments add quantization and Galician-resource citations, and App. A.8 expands the relationship to quantization attacks. Duplicate Sheshadri and Zou references are consolidated without removing the underlying works.

P1.justification: Most existing prose remains unchanged. v4 adds appendix subsections and cross-references, incorporates the earlier extended limitations discussion into Sec. 5, inserts a new Appendix B and renumbers subsequent appendices. Publication headers, coefficient names and reproducibility wording also receive limited edits.

P2.justification: Tables 11–20 substantially expand the numerical presentation with checkpoint comparisons, loss-weight sweeps, grouped precision/noise comparisons, Galician utility and keyword-presence controls. Figure 2 and Table 8 are repositioned relative to the narrative, with further appendix reflow. The existing figure graphics and original table results are preserved.

improvement.justification: The added checkpoint and regularization analyses, including independent FAB retrainings, improve understanding of when dormancy succeeds or fails. Galician and conditional experiments strengthen practical relevance, and direct code-access information helps reproducibility. These gains are tempered by broad screening recommendations supported only by the Llama-3.2-1B advertising tests and Appendix B's inconsistent 110% data mixture. The net improvement is useful but limited.
